speaker: Unknown
en: Hey, so I'm Anders.
zh: 嘿,我是 Anders。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm a developer advocate for Oracle AI Database.
zh: 我是 Oracle AI Database 的开发者布道师。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm talking about how we can approach agent memory as a systems problem, how we can take context and turn it into a real memory layer that is going to help your agents work better.
zh: 我要讲的是我们如何把智能体记忆当作一个系统问题来处理,如何把上下文变成一个真正的记忆层,来帮助你的智能体工作得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: When we're talking about agent memory, we're talking about composing memory retrieval, memory formation, and the persistent storage that's backing these memories.
zh: 当我们谈论智能体记忆时,我们谈的是组合记忆检索、记忆形成,以及支撑这些记忆的持久化存储。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we've probably all used different agents at this point, agents like Claude Code or Codex.
zh: 到现在为止,我们可能都用过不同的智能体,比如 Claude Code 或 Codex 这样的智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we've seen them work on a task and reread the same files over and over again.
zh: 我们见过它们处理一个任务,却一遍又一遍地重读同样的文件。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is because they have no knowledge of what has happened in the past.
zh: 这是因为它们对过去发生了什么毫无认知。

speaker: Unknown
en: Context windows are not memory.
zh: 上下文窗口不是记忆。

speaker: Unknown
en: They are the input for the current run and not a persistent experience.
zh: 它们是当前运行的输入,而不是持久的经验。

speaker: Unknown
en: If I have some agent session, let's say he's working on customer support tickets, he reads a bunch of documents, he runs a bunch of queries, he reproduces a failure, finds root cause, and does all this great valuable work that synthesizes a useful procedure, what happens at the end of the session?
zh: 如果我有一个智能体会话,比如说它在处理客户支持工单,它读了一堆文档,跑了一堆查询,复现了一个故障,找到根因,并完成了所有这些有价值的、能综合出有用流程的工作,那么会话结束时会发生什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: It's tossed away.
zh: 被扔掉了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is because there's no persistence.
zh: 这是因为没有持久化。

speaker: Unknown
en: Long later, another agent comes on, he works on a similar task, and he has to repeat all of this same work.
zh: 很久之后,另一个智能体上线了,它处理一个类似的任务,又不得不重复所有这些同样的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: So he's searching more documents, he's running more queries, and this is more opportunity for failure, more opportunity for hallucinations, and ultimately less fidelity.
zh: 于是它要搜索更多文档,跑更多查询,这带来了更多失败的机会、更多幻觉的机会,最终保真度更低。

speaker: Unknown
en: And memory really cannot begin until these useful experiences from our agents are transformed into managed state.
zh: 只有当智能体的这些有用经验被转化为受管理的状态时,记忆才真正开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: Larger context windows are also not the solution.
zh: 更大的上下文窗口也不是解决方案。

speaker: Unknown
en: We end up throwing more and more tokens.
zh: 我们最终会扔进越来越多的 token。

speaker: Unknown
en: The session goes longer.
zh: 会话变得更长。

speaker: Unknown
en: Compaction occurs.
zh: 压缩发生了。

speaker: Unknown
en: The useful signal that occurs for our agents is lost in a slew of other irrelevant information.
zh: 对智能体有用的信号被淹没在一堆其他无关信息之中。

speaker: Unknown
en: Likewise, scratch pads are workarounds.
zh: 同样,草稿板也只是权宜之计。

speaker: Unknown
en: So things like markdown files.
zh: 比如 markdown 文件这类东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: We start building large hierarchies of files, wikis, prompts.
zh: 我们开始构建庞大的文件层级、维基、提示词。

speaker: Unknown
en: These do help, but this is not governed recall.
zh: 这些确实有帮助,但这不是受治理的召回。

speaker: Unknown
en: Files do not scale in large multi-tenant environments.
zh: 文件在大型多租户环境中无法扩展。

speaker: Unknown
en: Tools like grep are extremely useful for finding data but they also don't scale well and it is not complex hybrid retrieval.
zh: 像 grep 这样的工具对查找数据极其有用,但它们同样无法很好地扩展,而且它也不是复杂的混合检索。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I feel like if we continue to the logical conclusion of trying to build a memory layer on top of files, we're gonna be building our own database.
zh: 我觉得如果我们继续沿着在文件之上构建记忆层的思路走到逻辑尽头,我们最终会是在自己造一个数据库。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I don't, you could just use a database.
zh: 而我不觉得——你直接用一个数据库就行了。

speaker: Unknown
en: In this presentation, this is unpacking the lessons that we've learned as a database vendor working with customers who are developing agent memory, customers who are solving real problems with agents and needing recall.
zh: 在这次演讲中,我要展开的是我们作为一家数据库厂商,与正在开发智能体记忆的客户、正在用智能体解决真实问题且需要召回能力的客户合作时所总结的经验教训。

speaker: Unknown
en: And where we're seeing modern agent memory systems converge is there's a pattern that's implementing memory formation, memory recall, evolution, and evaluation.
zh: 我们看到现代智能体记忆系统正在趋同的地方,是有一个模式在实现记忆形成、记忆召回、演化和评估。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when we form memories, these are distilled experiences, structured facts.
zh: 当我们形成记忆时,这些是提炼出的经验、结构化的事实。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is not a raw transcript dump.
zh: 这不是原始转写记录的倾倒。

speaker: Unknown
en: When we're recalling memories, hybrid retrieval is emerging as a dominant method.
zh: 当我们召回记忆时,混合检索正在成为主导方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a form of retrieval that fuses different types of search, so vector similarity search, lexical search, entity search over relational objects, graph traversals, and different signals over temporal data, recency, and feedback.
zh: 这是一种融合不同类型搜索的检索形式,包括向量相似度搜索、词法搜索、针对关系对象的实体搜索、图遍历,以及针对时间数据的不同信号——新近度和反馈。

speaker: Unknown
en: We also need consolidation in these systems, so duplicates can emerge.
zh: 我们在这些系统中还需要整合,因为重复项可能出现。

speaker: Unknown
en: We need to resolve conflicts.
zh: 我们需要解决冲突。

speaker: Unknown
en: The system needs to evolve over time, otherwise it becomes stale, irrelevant, and useless.
zh: 系统需要随时间演化,否则它会变得陈旧、不相关、毫无用处。

speaker: Unknown
en: Memories need element of temporality.
zh: 记忆需要时间性要素。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when was this created?
zh: 比如它是什么时候创建的?

speaker: Unknown
en: When was it accessed?
zh: 什么时候被访问的?

speaker: Unknown
en: How long is it valid for?
zh: 有效期是多久?

speaker: Unknown
en: It may only be valid for a certain time window.
zh: 它可能只在某个时间窗口内有效。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this all needs to come into regular feedback and evaluation.
zh: 而这一切都需要进入定期的反馈和评估。

speaker: Unknown
en: If I'm not measuring use, I'm not sending feedback into the memory layer, it's all gonna fall over.
zh: 如果我不度量使用情况,不把反馈送回记忆层,一切都会崩塌。

speaker: Unknown
en: Another
zh: 另一个

speaker: Unknown
en: Important piece is the governance controls.
zh: 重要的部分是治理控制。

speaker: Unknown
en: So secrets, personal information, that needs to be redacted before it hits the memory layer.
zh: 比如机密、个人信息,这些需要在进入记忆层之前被脱敏。

speaker: Unknown
en: Writes need to be scoped, scoped to the agent, scoped to the workflow, the team, the user.
zh: 写入需要有作用域限定,限定到智能体,限定到工作流、团队、用户。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is especially important in multi-tenant environments.
zh: 这在多租户环境中尤为重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: We need appropriate admin approvals, review, and ability to suppress stale or poison data.
zh: 我们需要适当的管理员审批、审查,以及抑制陈旧或被污染数据的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: When we walk through the memory loop, we have an agent session.
zh: 当我们走一遍记忆循环时,我们有一个智能体会话。

speaker: Unknown
en: It does some work, reads documents, run queries, synthesizes useful data.
zh: 它做一些工作,读取文档,运行查询,综合出有用的数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: After that session or during that session, a fact is created.
zh: 在那个会话之后或会话期间,会产生一个事实。

speaker: Unknown
en: We record that fact through redacting, enriching, storing it in the persistence layer.
zh: 我们通过脱敏、富化、存入持久层来记录那个事实。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then when another session comes along with related context, it can retrieve that fact and use it for context card reconstruction.
zh: 然后当另一个带有相关上下文的会话到来时,它可以检索那个事实并用它进行上下文卡片重构。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's using that fact that came from a prior art
zh: 所以它是利用那个来自先前工作的事实

speaker: Unknown
en: to make the next task easier.
zh: 来让下一个任务更容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's less work for the next agent to do.
zh: 这让下一个智能体要做的活更少。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if that agent uses the facts successfully, we can add feedback scores to that memory.
zh: 而如果那个智能体成功使用了这个事实,我们可以给那条记忆添加反馈分数。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we're adapting over time.
zh: 这样我们就在随时间不断适应。

speaker: Unknown
en: We get related data and new temporality.
zh: 我们拿到相关数据和新的时间性信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: We access it again.
zh: 我们再次访问它。

speaker: Unknown
en: We did something with it.
zh: 我们用它做了些什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, memory, it's invoked as a function by the agent runtime.
zh: 现在,记忆是被智能体运行时作为函数来调用的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it needs read, write, and storage layers.
zh: 所以它需要读、写和存储层。

speaker: Unknown
en: Your agent runtime can invoke the memory layer through things like hooks, MCP, skills, or other methods.
zh: 你的智能体运行时可以通过 hooks、MCP、skills 或其他方法来调用记忆层。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the memory layer API is exposing the read-write, the feedback, administrative APIs, and then talking to the storage platform or databases.
zh: 而记忆层 API 暴露读写、反馈、管理 API,然后与存储平台或数据库通信。

speaker: Unknown
en: The choice of database here, I think multi-model databases are especially useful because they allow you to not work with your rows, columns, vector embeddings, full text search, relational entities, graphs, episodes and facts, all in one place.
zh: 这里的数据库选型,我认为多模型数据库特别有用,因为它们让你不必分别处理行、列、向量嵌入、全文搜索、关系实体、图、情节和事实,而是全都在一个地方搞定。

speaker: Unknown
en: So your memory can live in a consolidated place with one database query connection.
zh: 所以你的记忆可以集中存放在一个地方,只需要一个数据库查询连接。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can do all sorts of hybrid search and return that data back.
zh: 我可以做各种混合搜索,把数据返回回来。

speaker: Unknown
en: What does the memory look like?
zh: 记忆长什么样?

speaker: Unknown
en: It's going to be typed, and you may have seen this model in different presentations or some form of it.
zh: 它是有类型的,你可能在不同的演示里见过这个模型或它的某种形式。

speaker: Unknown
en: This loosely comes from human memory.
zh: 它大致来自人类记忆。

speaker: Unknown
en: It can be applied to agents.
zh: 它可以应用于智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we have episodic memory.
zh: 所以我们有情节记忆。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is specific past events or slices of transcripts that the agents worked on.
zh: 这是特定的过往事件,或智能体处理过的转录片段。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have semantic memory.
zh: 我们有语义记忆。

speaker: Unknown
en: These are specific facts about our workflows, user preferences, and other entities.
zh: 这些是关于我们工作流、用户偏好和其他实体的具体事实。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have procedural memory.
zh: 我们有程序性记忆。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is like how we did a specific task or routine, maybe a build step.
zh: 这就像我们如何完成某个特定任务或例程,也许是一个构建步骤。

speaker: Unknown
en: These are reusable rules that agents are going to want to pull up again and again if there are repeating similar work.
zh: 这些是可复用的规则,如果有重复的类似工作,智能体会想要一次又一次地把它们调出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we have working state.
zh: 我们还有工作状态。

speaker: Unknown
en: Working state is like short-term memory.
zh: 工作状态就像短期记忆。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's what are we currently working on and that temporal data.
zh: 它是我们当前正在处理的东西以及那些时间性数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: It may only be valid for a certain time window and we may promote it to a different type of memory.
zh: 它可能只在某个时间窗口内有效,我们可能会把它提升为另一种类型的记忆。

speaker: Unknown
en: This helps us bucket into different areas and we can use different search techniques on these types of memory.
zh: 这帮助我们把记忆划分到不同区域,并且可以对这些类型的记忆使用不同的搜索技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: What does the storage schema look like for memory?
zh: 记忆的存储模式长什么样?

speaker: Unknown
en: So memory are typed objects plus lookup path.
zh: 记忆是有类型的对象加上查找路径。

speaker: Unknown
en: So our memory object is gonna have some ID like a primary key.
zh: 所以我们的记忆对象会有一个 ID,比如主键。

speaker: Unknown
en: It'll have its text content, JSON, tags, document data.
zh: 它会有文本内容、JSON、标签、文档数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: It'll have a vector embedding.
zh: 它会有一个向量嵌入。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have a vector created over the content with a vector index for similarity search.
zh: 我们对内容创建一个向量,并配有用于相似度搜索的向量索引。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ideally, we'll also have a text index to facilitate full text keyword search.
zh: 理想情况下,我们还会有一个文本索引,以支持全文关键词搜索。

speaker: Unknown
en: That combines with vector search.
zh: 它与向量搜索结合使用。

speaker: Unknown
en: We can have graph links to different edges.
zh: 我们可以有指向不同边的图链接。

speaker: Unknown
en: Memories can be related through an entity graph.
zh: 记忆可以通过实体图关联起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this memory is connected to this memory, which is connected to that memory.
zh: 所以这条记忆连接到这条记忆,这条记忆又连接到那条记忆。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's additional context that we can pull back during the search stage.
zh: 这是我们在搜索阶段可以拉回来的额外上下文。

speaker: Unknown
en: We can also have temporal facts.
zh: 我们还可以有时间性事实。

speaker: Unknown
en: When is this memory valid tool?
zh: 这条记忆什么时候有效?

speaker: Unknown
en: What was the last time that we used it?
zh: 我们上次使用它是什么时候？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then also, super importantly, audit events.
zh: 另外，还有超级重要的一点，审计事件。

speaker: Unknown
en: Who created this memory?
zh: 谁创建的这条记忆？

speaker: Unknown
en: What did they use it for?
zh: 他们用它来做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: The log of how it's been used and associated metadata.
zh: 它如何被使用的日志以及相关联的元数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: This should all be part of your storage schema when we're working with memories.
zh: 当我们在处理记忆时，这些都应该成为你存储模式的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: When we create memories, we want to intentionally form them.
zh: 当我们创建记忆时，我们要有意地去塑造它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: Good memories are very intentional, so we need to decide the lifecycle, the scope, the different relationships and associated metadata.
zh: 好的记忆是非常有意图的，所以我们需要决定生命周期、作用域、不同的关系以及相关联的元数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: When an agent runtime decides to create a memory, we should first start with redaction.
zh: 当智能体运行时决定创建一条记忆时，我们应该首先从脱敏开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: Redaction's very important as a first step because before I do embeddings, before I do enrichment, I want to strip out PII.
zh: 脱敏作为第一步非常重要，因为在我做 embeddings 之前，在我做富化之前，我想先把 PII 剥离掉。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't want secrets or irrelevant weird information slipping into the memory layer that's a recipe for disaster.
zh: 我不想让机密信息或不相关的奇怪信息溜进记忆层，那是灾难的根源。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we do redaction first.
zh: 所以我们先做脱敏。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then we can enrich the memory.
zh: 然后我们可以富化这条记忆。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is the memory related to?
zh: 这条记忆和什么相关？

speaker: Unknown
en: What is the metadata of the memory?
zh: 这条记忆的元数据是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: We can apply the scope to it.
zh: 我们可以对它应用作用域。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is the agent that worked on this memory?
zh: 处理这条记忆的是哪个智能体？

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the team?
zh: 是哪个团队？

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the organization?
zh: 是哪个组织？

speaker: Unknown
en: This helps bucket into specific areas, so I'm not getting memories in other sessions that are associated with other agents or workflows, which adds confusion.
zh: 这有助于分桶到特定的区域，这样我就不会在其他会话中拿到与其他智能体或工作流相关联的记忆，那种情况会造成混乱。

speaker: Unknown
en: We can do the embedding, so we create the vector of the content, and then we can form what's called the episode.
zh: 我们可以做 embedding，也就是为内容创建向量，然后我们可以形成所谓的 episode。

speaker: Unknown
en: These are the slices of the transcript that created the memory.
zh: 这些是创建该记忆的转写片段切片。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is good for provenance and additional context.
zh: 这对溯源和额外的上下文很有用。

speaker: Unknown
en: Any organization-specific policies here can also be applied, whatever you need for your specific use case, and then we can save down to the storage layer.
zh: 这里也可以应用任何组织特定的策略，你的具体用例需要什么都行，然后我们就可以保存到存储层。

speaker: Unknown
en: When we create memory, the individual memories can be quite compressed, so we take the transcript and we distill it down to that content and metadata and embedding and related stuff, but we can also create these episodes.
zh: 当我们创建记忆时，单条记忆可以被压缩得相当厉害，所以我们把转写稿蒸馏成内容、元数据、embedding 以及相关的东西，但我们也可以创建这些 episode。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we take the agent transcripts, we filter them, find candidates for these episodes, save the memory record and link it back.
zh: 所以我们拿到智能体的转写稿，过滤它们，找到这些 episode 的候选，保存记忆记录并把它链接回去。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can do this with relations, just straight up database relationships.
zh: 你可以用关系来做到这一点，就是直接的数据库关系。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can do it with graphs.
zh: 你也可以用图来做。

speaker: Unknown
en: I particularly like graphs because they allow a broader search here.
zh: 我特别喜欢图，因为它们允许在这里做更广泛的搜索。

speaker: Unknown
en: When we're talking about memory recall, that is how do we remember something, this is a retrieval problem, so a query problem on the storage layer.
zh: 当我们谈论记忆召回时，也就是我们如何记住某件事，这是一个检索问题，也就是存储层上的一个查询问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And with retrieval or recall, hybrid search is emerging as the dominant method of context reconstruction.
zh: 而在检索或召回方面，混合搜索正在成为上下文重建的主导方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this form of retrieval can fuse different search methods.
zh: 这种检索形式可以融合不同的搜索方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I can take vector similarity search.
zh: 所以我可以采用向量相似度搜索。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can take a full text keyword search.
zh: 我可以采用全文关键词搜索。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can take relational entities.
zh: 我可以采用关系实体。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can do graph traversal.
zh: 我可以做图遍历。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can take other feedback signals like importance, usefulness of the memory to yield more comprehensive results than one specific query branch alone.
zh: 我可以采用其他反馈信号，比如重要性、记忆的有用性，从而得到比单一查询分支更全面的结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like if I was only doing similarity search, I only get the most similar results according to the embedding model that I'm using.
zh: 比如，如果我只做相似度搜索，我只能得到根据我所使用的 embedding 模型来说最相似的结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: In general, this has not been enough.
zh: 总体而言，这一直都不够。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have all these different query branches, different types of memory.
zh: 我们有这些不同的查询分支、不同类型的记忆。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can decide which ones you want to do.
zh: 你可以决定你想做哪些。

speaker: Unknown
en: Things like facts, you might not want similarity.
zh: 像事实这类东西，你可能不想要相似度。

speaker: Unknown
en: You might just want to do an exact ID match on a fact.
